co_west_side_6.blurb: The west face of South Gateway Rock in Garden of the Gods, Colorado Springs, looking toward Pikes Peak. Ten routes, mostly traditional lines with a couple of bolted routes and one top-rope. Difficulty runs from an easy fourth-class gully up to the low 5.12s, with most of the climbing between 5.8 and 5.11. Parts of the face are on firmer Fountain sandstone than is typical of the park, though the red rock still sheds the odd piece, so wear a helmet and watch the belay spot. Climbs include a classic three-pitch crack and chimney line. A short walk on established trails from the west side gets you to the base.

co_1014_boulder.blurb: A single sandstone boulder among the Nine Mile boulders in Unaweep Canyon, near Grand Junction, tucked in with the Dave Loves Donna group. Ten problems, all on the boulder's south side, which carries some striking huecos. The grades stay friendly to middle-range climbers: a couple of V1s, several V2s, a trio of V3s and a single V4, so it suits someone working up through the V2 to V3 range. Expect good quality, hard moves rather than height or crowds. One problem, Just Getting Started, is the standout and well worth a look if you are in the canyon.
co_1014_boulder.parking_note: Leave the car at the Dave Loves Donna pulloff, on the side of the road about six miles from the US 50 and CO 141 junction, then cross the road on foot.
co_1014_boulder.approach: Cross the road from the pulloff, pass Lavoe Boulder, and continue north for roughly four minutes.

co_aprons_the.blurb: Three big alpine slabs above Summit Lake on Mt. Blue Sky, the peak formerly called Mt. Evans. Climbing here is multi-pitch alpine trad, with all ten routes between 5.5 and 5.9, with 5.7 the most common. The left apron is the longest, shadiest and most demanding, the middle one holds moderate slabs with decent protection, and the right is the gentlest but thinnest on gear. Rock quality is good and takes a standard alpine rack. Plan for snow in early season, an early start, and an eye on afternoon storms, as there is no cover on the slabs.

co_big_five_the.blurb: The upper cliff of the Safari area in Clear Creek Canyon near Golden, between tunnels 5 and 6. Ten bolted single-pitch sport routes, roughly 40 to 100 feet long, on steep rock with big holds. Grades are mostly moderate, from an easy starter up through the high 5.8s and 5.9s, which makes it a good place for newer leaders. The area is known as one of the sunnier spots in the canyon and sheds snow quickly. Every route starts from Sun Tan Ledge, reached by climbing one of the lower slab routes or by a gully on the left and an exposed traverse. Bring a brush and a helmet; watch for cactus.

co_becker_wall.blurb: A compact wall on Palisade Mountain in Big Thompson Canyon, west of Loveland and near Estes Park. About ten routes, mostly traditional with a few bolted lines and two top-rope options, plus an unclimbed project. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.11, with a spread of easier routes and three at 5.11. The wall is short, around 45 feet, and faces south, so it sits in sun all day: pleasant in winter and hot in summer. Descent is by walking off or rappelling from natural anchors. Poison ivy is common on the hillside approach.
